---
title: Configuration
description: Reference for the Latet configuration file.
---

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_reference.py from the code: do not edit by hand. -->

Latet reads `config.yaml` from your user configuration folder. `latet global-install` writes it, and
the dashboard's **Rules** page changes it. After editing it by hand, `latet reload` applies it
to the running daemon (a new `port` needs `latet stop` and `latet start`).

| System | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\latet\config.yaml` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/latet/config.yaml` |
| Linux | `~/.config/latet/config.yaml` |

An example:

```yaml
profile: balanced
terms:
- value: Project Falcon
  type: PROJECT
allow_values:
- admin@example.com
policies:
  PHONE: redact
history: full
```

## Keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | `balanced` or `max` or `secrets` | `balanced` | Protection profile: `balanced`, `max` or `secrets`. |
| `port` | number | `5283` | Local port of the daemon (it listens on 127.0.0.1 only). |
| `phone_regions` | list of text | `[IT, US, GB]` | Countries whose phone numbers are recognised without an international prefix. |
| `id_regions` | list of text | `[IT, US, GB]` | Countries whose national ID and tax numbers are recognised (the `max` profile: all of them): `BE`, `CA`, `CH`, `DE`, `ES`, `FI`, `FR`, `GB`, `IT`, `LV`, `NL`, `PL`, `PT`, `SE`, `US`. VAT numbers of 30 European countries are recognised whatever this says. |
| `pii` | list of text | not set | Personal-data types to detect; not set means the base types and the ID numbers of `id_regions`, and a list is used as it is. |
| `include_private_ips` | true or false | not set | Also mask private IP addresses (10.x, 192.168.x...); on in `max` by default. |
| `disabled_secret_rules` | list of text | `[]` | gitleaks rule ids to turn off, such as `generic-api-key`. |
| `terms` | list of object | `[]` | Your own values to always mask. |
| `recognizers` | list of objects (see below) | `[]` | Your own recognizers: a pattern, check digits and keywords for each (see below). An entry with a mistake is turned off and reported, and kept as it is. |
| `allow_values` | list of text | `[]` | Values never to mask (not sensitive). |
| `allow_patterns` | list of text | `[]` | Regular expressions (RE2) of values never to mask. |
| `policies` | map of text to `mask` or `redact` or `allow` | `{}` | Per type: `mask` (reversible surrogate), `redact` (one way, never restored) or `allow`. |
| `identity` | object | see below | This machine's identity. |
| `capture_dir` | path | not set | Debugging only: write raw exchanges (credentials redacted) to this directory. |
| `history` | `full` or `metadata` or `off` | `full` | What the dashboard keeps of each exchange: `full` (masked text and answers), `metadata` (counts, timings, flags; no text) or `off`. |
| `retention_days` | number | `14` | Days the dashboard history is kept. |
| `auto_mode_review` | `block`, `allow-identity` or object | `block` | Claude Code's auto mode reviewer is sent your OS user name and the paths of your home and working directories, plus any host name or git author in your CLAUDE.md or in the action. A review that would carry a blocked detail is stopped, and auto mode cannot approve that action: Claude Code refuses it as if its reviewer were unavailable. `block` blocks every detail, `allow-identity` lets every detail through, and the keys below choose one by one. Secrets and personal data never reach the reviewer. |
| `ner` | `auto` or `off` | `auto` | Local name and address detection: `auto` uses it once installed (`latet ner install`), `off` never does. |
| `ocr` | `auto` or `off` | `auto` | The text in images: `auto` reads it once the models are installed (`latet ocr install`) and masks what it finds, `off` never does (images are then sent as they are, and flagged). |
| `data` | `normal` or `strict` | not set | `strict` masks every value of tool outputs that are tables (psql, CSV, TSV, markdown, HTML, a browser's snapshot), JSON or `key=value`, column and key names aside; fields set `mask: false` stay in clear. Outputs of tools that read files are left alone unless `data_files` names the file, and so are web search results and pages (public content, not your data) unless `data_tools` names their tool or `data_hosts` their address. Not set: the profile decides, `strict` with `max` and `normal` with the others. |
| `data_tools` | list of text | `[]` | The tools and MCP servers strict data mode covers (`*` patterns, such as `mcp__postgres__*`); empty: every tool but those that read files. |
| `data_files` | list of text | `[]` | The files strict data mode covers when a tool reads them: path patterns such as `*.json`, `**/*.csv`, `exports/**` or `.env*` (`*` for any characters, in any case; a pattern without a slash names a file by its name). Each value is found by the file's format: JSON, tables, `.env` and properties, YAML. A markdown file only when a pattern names markdown (`*.md`), and then only its tables. A file named is data whether strict data mode is on or off. |
| `data_hosts` | list of text | `[]` | The web addresses strict data mode covers when a web tool fetches them: host patterns such as `api.internal.example.com` or `*.salesforce.com`. An address named is data whether strict data mode is on or off. |
| `fields` | list of object | `[]` | Rules for the values of single fields of tables, JSON and `key=value`. |
| `dump_guard` | number | not set | Withhold a tool output that holds more personal values (e-mails, phone numbers, names, ID numbers...) than this: the model is told why instead. Not set or 0: never. |
| `images` | `allow` or `mask` or `block` | `allow` | `allow` sends images, with their text masked once the text recognition models are installed (`latet ocr install`); `mask` sends only images whose text was read and masked, and no documents; `block` sends no images or documents. The max profile sends none either, unless this says `mask`. |
| `llm_review` | object | see below | The local reviewer: a language model on your own server that reads what the detectors left in clear (see below). |
| `live_review` | object | see below | The Live Reviewer: every new text waits for your approval in the dashboard (see below). |
| `projects` | list of object | `[]` | Your own settings for single projects, on top of these and of the project's `latet.yaml` (see below). |
| `upstreams` | list of object | `[]` | Where agents' requests go after Latet, besides Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter: your company's gateway, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry. `latet claude`, `latet codex` and `global-install` add the ones they read from your agents' settings (see below). |

## `terms` items

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | text | required | The text to mask wherever it appears: a client, a project code name, a domain. It needs a letter or a digit. |
| `type` | text | `CUSTOM` | The label shown for it, such as CLIENT or PROJECT. |
| `case_sensitive` | true or false | `false` | Match the exact case only. |
| `whole_word` | true or false | `true` | Match whole words only (not inside longer words). |

## `identity`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | true or false | `true` | Mask this machine's identity (detected each time Latet starts, when the fields below are empty). |
| `usernames` | list of text | `[]` | OS user names, masked inside home paths. |
| `hostname` | text | not set | This machine's host name. |
| `hostnames` | list of text | `[]` | Other host names of yours, masked as `hostname` is (on a Latet server, each of your computers'). |
| `full_name` | text | not set | Your name, as in your git author. |
| `emails` | list of text | `[]` | Your email addresses, as in your git author. |

## `recognizers` items

See [Custom recognizers](../../concepts/custom-recognizers/) for how to write one, and
`latet rules test` to check it.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | required | Lower case letters, digits and hyphens; unique. |
| `type` | text | not set | The type shown for it, in capitals; the name in capitals when not set. |
| `description` | text | `''` | What it finds, in words. |
| `pattern` | text | required | An RE2 regular expression. A group named `value` picks the part to mask. |
| `checksum` | text or object | not set | Check digits the value must pass: luhn, iban, mod97-10, mod11-10, ean, verhoeff, damm, or a weighted sum. |
| `context` | object | not set | Keywords that must be near the value. |
| `examples` | object | see below | Invented examples, checked on every load. |
| `class` | `custom` or `secret` | `custom` | `custom`, or `secret` to treat it like a password (never let through, blocks a request). |
| `policy` | `mask` or `redact` or `allow` | not set | `mask`, `redact` or `allow`; `policies` wins. |
| `surrogate` | `shape` or object | `shape` | `shape` (same length and kinds of characters), or `{keep: N}`. |
| `min_length` | number | `1` | Shorter values are skipped. |
| `enabled` | true or false | `true` | `false` keeps the rule in the file, turned off. |

## `fields` items

A rule for the values of one field of a tool's output: a column of a table, a JSON key or path,
the key of `key=value`. Of your rules (your own settings for a project first, then the global rules)
the first that matches a field applies, and a project's `latet.yaml`'s first too: the stricter of
the two, yours when as strict. See
[Production data](../../concepts/production-data/).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | required | The field: a column name, a JSON key or path (`items[].sku`), or the key of `key=value`; `*` matches any characters, and case does not matter. |
| `type` | text | not set | The type its values are masked as (`FIELD` when not set). |
| `mask` | true or false | `true` | `false` keeps its values in clear in strict data mode (only in your own settings). |
| `secret` | true or false | `false` | Its values are secrets: one in clear blocks the request. |

## `llm_review`

The local reviewer: a language model on your own OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM
Studio) reads what the detectors left in clear and masks what it finds. It runs on this machine only, it
can add to what is masked but never take anything away, and a text it read once is not read again.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | true or false | `false` | Ask the local reviewer. |
| `url` | text | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` | Its OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio): on this machine, or on another machine of yours with `remote: true`. |
| `remote` | true or false | `false` | The server is yours, on another machine: Latet sends it the original texts. Outside your local network its address must be https. |
| `model` | text | not set | The model's id on the server (not set: the first it lists). |
| `api_key_env` | text | `LATET_LLM_API_KEY` | The environment variable holding the server's API key, if any. Without it, the key saved from the dashboard or with `latet llm key` is used (kept in the operating system's credential store). |
| `api_key_file` | text | not set | Or a file holding the key (the key itself never goes in this file). |
| `inline` | list of `user_text` or `attachment` or `system` or `tool_result` or `tool_input` or `tool_description` or `image_text` | `[user_text, attachment, system, tool_result, image_text]` | What is reviewed before it leaves: by default everything the model did not write (your prompts and attachments, its instructions, what its tools fetch). |
| `budget_ms` | number | not set | How long a request may wait for its review (not set: as long as it takes). |
| `on_failure` | `stop` or `send` | `stop` | When a review cannot be done (the server is off, too slow for `budget_ms`, or its answer is not to be trusted): `stop` the request, or `send` it masked as the detectors did. |
| `background` | true or false | `true` | Review after it is sent what is not reviewed before: what it finds is masked from the next request on. |
| `slots` | number | not set | Reviews the server runs side by side (not set: what llama.cpp says, or 1). |
| `block` | true or false | `false` | Let the reviewer stop a request whose text must not leave even masked (a whole medical record). |
| `auto_mask` | list of `person` or `address` or `phone` or `email` or `id` or `health` or `sensitive` or `financial` or `secret` or `org` or `confidential` | `[person, address, email, phone, secret, health, financial]` | Categories it masks by itself; the others are shown in the dashboard as suggestions. |
| `chunk_chars` | number | `7000` | Long texts are reviewed in pieces of about this many characters, 16,384 at most: the longest value Latet keeps, so that what the reviewer finds in a piece is always kept. A larger setting is read as 16,384. |
| `certificate` | text | not set | The SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's certificate you trust, for a self-signed one on another machine of yours: `latet llm trust`, or *Trust it* in the dashboard. Only that certificate is accepted. |
| `images` | true or false | `false` | Show the reviewer the images too, with the text read in them (its model must see images: llama.cpp with `--mmproj`). It finds what text recognition missed; a value it sees but Latet cannot place in the image withholds the image. |
| `guidance` | text | not set | Your guidance, added after Latet's own instructions to the reviewer: what else is confidential in your work, or what to leave alone (at most 2000 characters). It applies to the texts reviewed from then on. It is sent to the reviewer's server with every review: describe kinds of values, and keep the confidential ones themselves in `terms`. |

## `live_review`

The Live Reviewer: every new text an agent is about to send waits for your approval in the dashboard.
You approve it, mask more in it, or stop it; you can only add masking. See
[Live Reviewer](../../concepts/live-review/).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | true or false | `false` | Every new text waits for your approval in the dashboard: you confirm it, or mask more first. |
| `kinds` | list of `user_text` or `attachment` or `system` or `tool_result` or `tool_input` or `tool_description` or `image_text` | `[user_text, attachment, system, tool_result, image_text]` | What waits for you: by default everything the model did not write (your prompts and attachments, its instructions, what its tools fetch). |
| `auto_approve_clean` | true or false | `false` | Send without asking a text in which neither Latet nor the local reviewer found anything. |
| `timeout_s` | number | not set | How long a text waits for you; when the time is up it is not sent (not set: until you answer). |

## `auto_mode_review`

One choice per detail of your identity that Claude Code's auto mode reviewer may receive.
`block` and `allow-identity` set every detail at once, and are kept that way in the file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user_name` | `block` or `allow` or `surrogate` | `block` | Your OS user name, which the reviewer is told as its *User identity*. `surrogate` gives Claude Code your user name's surrogate instead (in `USERNAME` and `USER`), so the reviewer sees the same fake name as the model. |
| `paths` | `block` or `allow` | `block` | Your user folder's name in the paths of your home and working directories. |
| `host_name` | `block` or `allow` | `block` | This machine's host name. |
| `git_author` | `block` or `allow` | `block` | Your name and email, as in your git author. |

## `projects` items

Your own settings for one project, on top of the keys above and of the project's `latet.yaml`:
a value replaces the global one, a list is added to it. See [Projects](../../concepts/projects/).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | `balanced` or `max` or `secrets` | not set | The profile in this project. |
| `pii` | list of text | `[]` | Personal-data types to detect, besides the global ones. |
| `id_regions` | list of text | `[]` | Countries whose national ID and tax numbers to recognise, besides the global ones. |
| `phone_regions` | list of text | `[]` | Countries whose phone numbers to recognise without a prefix, besides the global ones. |
| `include_private_ips` | true or false | not set | Also mask private IP addresses. |
| `ner` | `auto` or `off` | not set | Local name and address detection. |
| `terms` | list of object | `[]` | Values to always mask in this project. |
| `recognizers` | list of map of text to Any | `[]` | Recognizers for this project (a name or a type a global one uses turns the entry off; a repository file's of the name or the type of one of yours applies under a name and a type of its own, such as `badge-repo` and `BADGE_REPO`, both types at the stricter of the two policies). |
| `allow_values` | list of text | `[]` | Values never to mask in this project. |
| `allow_patterns` | list of text | `[]` | Regular expressions (RE2) of values never to mask in this project. |
| `policies` | map of text to `mask` or `redact` or `allow` | `{}` | Per type: `mask`, `redact` or `allow`. |
| `disabled_secret_rules` | list of text | `[]` | gitleaks rule ids to turn off in this project. |
| `data` | `normal` or `strict` | not set | `strict` masks every value of tool outputs that are tables, JSON or `key=value`. |
| `data_tools` | list of text | `[]` | The tools strict data mode covers (`*` patterns), besides the global ones. |
| `data_files` | list of text | `[]` | The files strict data mode covers when a tool reads them (path patterns such as `*.json`), besides the global ones. |
| `data_hosts` | list of text | `[]` | The web addresses strict data mode covers (host patterns such as `*.salesforce.com`), besides the global ones. |
| `fields` | list of object | `[]` | Rules for the values of single fields. |
| `dump_guard` | number | not set | Withhold a tool output with more personal values than this (0: never). |
| `images` | `allow` or `mask` or `block` | not set | `mask` sends images only with their text read and masked, `block` sends no images or documents. |
| `ocr` | `auto` or `off` | not set | Reading the text in images. |
| `llm_review` | `off` or `background` or `inline` | not set | How much the local reviewer reads here, when it is on: `off`, `background` or `inline`. |
| `live_review` | true or false | not set | Whether new texts wait for your approval in the dashboard in this project. |
| `review_images` | true or false | not set | Whether the local reviewer is shown the images in this project. Yours alone: a repository file cannot set it. |
| `review_guidance` | text | not set | Your guidance to the local reviewer for this project, added after your global `llm_review.guidance` (at most 2000 characters). Yours alone: a repository file cannot set it. |
| `path` | text | required | The project's folder; its subfolders are part of it. |
| `enabled` | true or false | `true` | `false` turns Latet off in this project: nothing is masked or blocked, and surrogates already in a conversation are still restored. |

## `upstreams` items

Where an agent's requests go after Latet, when they go to your company's gateway, Azure OpenAI or
Microsoft Foundry rather than straight to the provider: requests to `http://127.0.0.1:5283/<name>/...`
go to its address. Changing a destination's address, or removing it, waits for your approval when it
does not come from the dashboard. See [Company endpoints](../../agents/company-endpoints/).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | required | Its route: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (`llm-acme-com`), and none of Latet's own (`anthropic`, `openai`, `chatgpt`, `openrouter`, `gemini`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `backend-api`). |
| `url` | text | required | The address requests go to, such as `https://llm.acme.com`: https outside your local network, no user, password or query in it. |
| `agent` | `claude` or `codex` | not set | The agent whose settings Latet read it from; not set: written by you. |

## The project file: `latet.yaml`

A project's own settings, in its repository, shared with everyone who works on it. It may set
these keys, and only to add protection: anything else in it is ignored, and `latet project
check` says what and why. Its [JSON Schema](https://docs.latet.ai/project.schema.json) lets editors check it.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | `balanced` or `max` or `secrets` | not set | The profile in this project. |
| `pii` | list of text | `[]` | Personal-data types to detect, besides the global ones. |
| `id_regions` | list of text | `[]` | Countries whose national ID and tax numbers to recognise, besides the global ones. |
| `phone_regions` | list of text | `[]` | Countries whose phone numbers to recognise without a prefix, besides the global ones. |
| `include_private_ips` | true or false | not set | Also mask private IP addresses. |
| `ner` | `auto` or `off` | not set | Local name and address detection. |
| `terms` | list of object | `[]` | Values to always mask in this project. |
| `recognizers` | list of map of text to Any | `[]` | Recognizers for this project (a name or a type a global one uses turns the entry off; a repository file's of the name or the type of one of yours applies under a name and a type of its own, such as `badge-repo` and `BADGE_REPO`, both types at the stricter of the two policies). |
| `policies` | map of text to `mask` or `redact` or `allow` | `{}` | Per type: `mask`, `redact` or `allow`. |
| `data` | `normal` or `strict` | not set | `strict` masks every value of tool outputs that are tables, JSON or `key=value`. |
| `data_files` | list of text | `[]` | The files strict data mode covers when a tool reads them (path patterns such as `*.json`), besides the global ones. |
| `data_hosts` | list of text | `[]` | The web addresses strict data mode covers (host patterns such as `*.salesforce.com`), besides the global ones. |
| `fields` | list of object | `[]` | Rules for the values of single fields. |
| `dump_guard` | number | not set | Withhold a tool output with more personal values than this (0: never). |
| `images` | `allow` or `mask` or `block` | not set | `mask` sends images only with their text read and masked, `block` sends no images or documents. |
| `ocr` | `auto` or `off` | not set | Reading the text in images. |
| `llm_review` | `off` or `background` or `inline` | not set | How much the local reviewer reads here, when it is on: `off`, `background` or `inline`. |

## Server settings

An instance reads these keys from `server.yaml`, selected with `latet server run --config FILE`
or `LATET_SERVER_CONFIG`. Its `LATET_SERVER_*` variables override the file; the master-key file
uses `LATET_MASTER_KEY_FILE`. These are deployment settings, separate from the settings the server
shares (`latet server config`) and each identity's own settings and rules (the server dashboard).
See [Server operations](../../concepts/server-operations/) for storage, TLS, keys and limits.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | text | required | The address people use, such as https://latet.acme.lan (http on this machine only). |
| `database_url` | text | required | PostgreSQL: postgresql://user:password@host:5432/latet, with ?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=... off this machine. |
| `valkey_url` | text | required | Valkey or Redis: redis://host:6379/0 on this machine, rediss://:password@host off it. |
| `master_key_file` | path | not set | The master key (LATET_MASTER_KEY gives it too). |
| `host` | text | `0.0.0.0` | Where an instance listens. |
| `port` | number | `5283` | The port an instance listens on. |
| `certificate` | path | not set | TLS at the instance (else at the load balancer). |
| `key` | path | not set | The private key of the instance's certificate, in a private file. |
| `log_format` | `text` or `json` | `text` | How the log's lines are written on the standard output: text or json. |
| `log_level` | text | `info` | What Latet's own lines say from: one of debug, info, warning, error. |
| `metrics_token_file` | path | not set | A file holding the token Prometheus asks the metrics with: no file, no metrics. |
| `reviewer_key_file` | path | not set | A file holding the local reviewer's own API key, never another secret, read once at start. Every identity's reviewer on this server sends it to the shared reviewer's address set by the administrators, over https or on this machine. The server reads no variable, keyring or saved key for it. |
| `metrics_host` | text | `127.0.0.1` | Where an instance answers Prometheus: an address only Prometheus reaches. |
| `metrics_port` | number | `7283` | The port where an instance answers Prometheus, with metrics_token_file: never the instance's own port (port). |
| `database_password_file` | path | not set | A file holding PostgreSQL's password. |
| `database_connect_timeout` | number | `5` | Seconds PostgreSQL has to answer a new connection before it is given up. |
| `database_pool` | number | `10` | How many connections to PostgreSQL an instance keeps at most, for every identity's work; three tenths of them (one at least) may be held by applications calls that keep their new values in one transaction, the others keeping each value at once. Raise it, with PostgreSQL's max_connections, for an instance that masks for many new keys at once. |
| `database_private_network` | true or false | `false` | Reach PostgreSQL over a network that only the instances share, with no checked TLS. |
| `valkey_password_file` | path | not set | A file holding Valkey's password. |
| `valkey_unauthenticated` | true or false | `false` | Reach a Valkey that asks no password: only one nothing else can reach. |
| `valkey_private_network` | true or false | `false` | Reach Valkey over a network that only the instances share, with no checked TLS. |
| `max_request_mb` | number | `32` | The largest request body, in MiB. |
| `apps_request_mb` | number | `8` | The largest request body of the applications API (/_latet/apps/v1), in MiB: past it, 413. max_request_mb bounds it as well, when it is lower. |
| `requests_in_flight` | number | `16` | How many requests one identity may have in flight on an instance, counted separately for its destinations (HTTP or WebSocket turns), dashboard, bridge and applications API: past each limit, 429. Long polls and streams have their own limits. |
| `vault_limit` | number | `200000` | How many values one identity's vault may hold. |
| `key_working_values` | number | `5000` | How many values of an API key's vault an instance keeps in memory, those used last: every other one is found in PostgreSQL as a text needs it. |
| `key_held_secrets` | number | `1000` | How many secrets of an API key's vault that no word of a text finds glued to letters or digits (one run of 16 characters or fewer, or a short word at its edge) an instance holds in memory for good, the newest: an older one is found in PostgreSQL when nothing is glued to it, or one side only when it has seven characters or more. Each one held takes about 2.2 KB on every instance, and every text the key masks or unmasks is read for it: raise it for a key that sees many short secrets, such as a session token in each log line. |
| `history_limit_mb` | number | `1024` | How many MiB one identity's history may keep: past it, its oldest exchanges go. |
| `admin_token_days` | number | `90` | How many days a new administration token lasts (`--never` opts out). |
| `forwarded_allow_ips` | text | `127.0.0.1` | The proxy's addresses, whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed (never *, nor a network wider than /8 for IPv4 or /32 for IPv6). |
| `valkey_connections` | number | `100` | How many connections to Valkey an instance keeps at most: past them a call waits for one, five seconds at most. |
| `audit_retention_days` | number | `365` | How many days the administration log keeps an entry. |
| `ocr_readers` | number | `2` | How many text recognitions an instance keeps, each reading one image at a time, the processors this instance may use shared among them (never more readers than processors): each holds its models in memory (0.05 GB at rest; the first brings ONNX Runtime, 0.7 GB), and up to 0.9 GB more while it reads a large screenshot. |
| `ocr_read_seconds` | float | `30.0` | How long one image's text may take to read: past it the image is withheld, or the request that only carries it stopped. |
| `ocr_wait_seconds` | float | `35.0` | How long a read waits at most, for its identity's other read and then for a text recognition: past it, as past the read's time. Never shorter than ocr_read_seconds. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `LATET_CONFIG` | Read the configuration from this file instead. |
| `LATET_DATA_DIR` | Keep the vault, the dashboard history and the logs in this folder. |
| `LATET_TRUSTED_ACCOUNTS` | Windows accounts or groups, by name (`COMPUTER\name`, `DOMAIN\name`, `name`) or by SID (`S-1-5-…` or `*S-1-5-…`), separated by `;` or `,`, that may change the parent folders of Latet's data folder as the Administrators may (the direct members of the local Administrators group may, with no setting); never the data folder itself or a folder in it. Read from the registry alone, your user environment and the computer's, as `setx`, the system settings and group policy write them: a value set only in a terminal session counts for nothing. A name Windows does not find, or an account that is not one of this computer, a domain, Entra ID or a service, trusts nothing; `latet doctor` says so, and lists the accounts trusted and where the variable is set. It changes nothing on Linux and macOS, where the folder checks are by owner and mode. |
| `LATET_ROOT_KEY` | The vault's root key (base64), instead of the OS keyring. |
| `LATET_BRIDGE_TOKEN` | Claude plugin token: local bridge token or connected computer's personal token. |
| `LATET_PORT` | The daemon's port, over `port` in the file (the container is given its port this way). |
| `LATET_HOST` | The address to listen on; anything but this machine only with `LATET_CONTAINER=1`. |
| `LATET_CONTAINER` | `1` in the container image: the commands that change your computer refuse. |
| `LATET_KEYRING` | `off` keeps the root key in `root.key` in the data folder and saves no credential in the OS keyring; an older copy found there makes `latet connect` refuse until `latet disconnect` revokes and removes it, and a locked keychain may ask to be unlocked. |
| `LATET_ROOT_KEY_FILE` | Read the root key (base64) from this file, such as a Docker secret. |
| `LATET_AUTOSTART` | `0` in Claude Code's settings: the plugin does not start a daemon of its own. |
| `LATET_CONNECTION` | Read this computer's private server connection record from this file instead of `connection.yaml` in its data folder. It holds server, identity and certificate-pin metadata; the personal token is stored separately. Keep the record private. |
| `LATET_SERVER_URL` | The public URL of a server instance; also the default server address for administration commands when `--server` is absent. |
| `LATET_SERVER_FINGERPRINT` | The server certificate's fingerprint for administration commands when `--fingerprint` is absent. Verify it through a trusted channel before using it. |
| `LATET_SERVER_ADMIN_TOKEN` | An administration token from a CI or container secret store, bound to `LATET_SERVER_URL`. Keep it out of an agent user's shell environment; use a hidden prompt or `--admin-token-file` on that computer. |

## JSON Schema

The file's [JSON Schema](https://docs.latet.ai/config.schema.json) (also `latet config schema`) lets editors complete and
check it: `latet global-install` and the dashboard write a `# yaml-language-server` line at the top for
that. `latet config validate` checks a file, recognizers included.
